prompt: On the unit circle, the angle $90^\circ$ lands on the point $(0, 1)$. Sine is the HEIGHT UP. What is $\sin 90^\circ$?
hint: Sine is the SECOND number in the point $(x, y)$ — how high up you are.

hints.text: Sine is the SECOND number in the point $(x, y)$ — how high up you are.
The point at $90^\circ$ is $(0, 1)$, so the height is $1$.

explanation: A quarter turn from the right edge takes you straight to the top of the circle.
The top point is $(0, 1)$: zero across, one unit up.
Sine reads the height, so $\sin 90^\circ = 1$. This is the biggest sine can ever be.

alternativeExplanations.title: Picture the clock hand
steps: Aim a hand of length 1 straight UP, like a clock hand at 12. That is the 90° direction.
The tip is 0 units across and 1 unit up. The up number IS the sine, so sin 90° = 1.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sine can never beat 1
steps: The circle has radius 1, so no point on it is more than 1 unit above the centre.
The very top is exactly 1 unit up, and you reach it at 90°. So sin 90° = 1 is the ceiling for sine.
